data.hypothesis: The three distinct prior OpenMP programs are correct and faster in aggregate than the serial baseline, but their timings do not isolate one- versus four-core behavior and all use loop-based work sharing. This candidate tests whether explicitly assigning balanced, contiguous row blocks from each call's actual OpenMP team reduces scheduling overhead while retaining locality. It uses a separate region per timestep for a one-thread budget and one synchronized persistent region for larger budgets; controller measurements must determine whether either effect matters.

memory_lessons.applicability: Only the aggregate timings visible in this campaign; they do not isolate thread counts or region overhead.
memory_lessons.claim: The serial baseline is valid at 0.4575 s, while three distinct prior T1 OpenMP programs are valid at 0.2292–0.2396 s. These results do not establish how much comes from parallel scaling versus region reuse at either official thread setting.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure the explicit contiguous-block variant with the official one- and four-core settings and compare it under the same protocol with the baseline and prior row-loop candidates.

data.notes: This proposal preserves the six-step ping-pong update and untouched boundary cells, and routes small workloads through the serial implementation. No commands or measurements were run here; the controller should verify small cases and n=256, then measure the official one- and four-core settings.
transformations: Retained the original stencil arithmetic, six-step ping-pong parity, initialization, and boundary-write bounds while factoring computation into a row kernel.
Added explicit balanced contiguous static row-block ownership based on omp_get_thread_num() and omp_get_num_threads(), without changing global OpenMP settings.

Used a parallel region per timestep for larger one-thread workloads and one persistent team with a barrier between timesteps for larger thread budgets; retained a serial path for small workloads and nonpositive budgets.
